text:
Mia: quick proposal — shift more of the high-cardinality mitigation to the ingestion/indexer layer instead of only exporter scrubbing. goal: simpler downstream queries + cheaper retention.
Lee: do you mean hashing & salting at ingest? or throwing away attributes entirely?
Mia: hashing+salt at ingest. two variants: 1) strong salted hash kept for 90 days for debugging, stored in ephemeral index; 2) a short prefix/signature (8 hex chars) persisted long-term for aggregation.
Anika: 8 hex feels small — collision risk? what's our collision budget for routing policies/deduping?
Mia: noted. we ran a quick sim w/ current cardinality — prefix collisions at 8 hex are ~1e-6 for our cardinalities. safe for dashboard-level rollups.
Sam: longer-term concern: if we salt at ingest we need a key rotation plan. otherwise backfills + re-ingest will mismatch.
Mia: agreed — plan is salt with version id stored in an adjacent non-queryable meta attr. rotation = monthly; old salts kept to re-hash for backfills in a controlled job.
Jorge: sounds reasonable. how does this interact with prompt hashing vs storing raw prompt? Product wants some raws for troubleshooting customer escalations.
Mia: we propose keeping raw prompt in a short retention tier (7d) encrypted and access-gated. after 7d we only keep prompt_signature + length + token_count.
ProductSRE: 7d seems small for enterprise investigations. can we make a TTL override via ticket + audit log?
Anika: implement admin-unseal flow: short-term access to raw within a bounded window, logged and requires two approvals. fits compliance.
Sam: related: exporters currently add request.id and user.id as-is. we should canonicalize them to hashed form before they hit OTLP collector. less dependent on downstream scrubbing.
Lee: would that break tracing joins across services? request.id is used to correlate logs + traces. If we hash on ingest, we must ensure consistent salt across all telemetry types and regions.
Mia: correct. policy: same global salt per deployment + deterministic hash function. we still propagate unhashed id within internal network headers for live joins, but telemetry pipeline only persists hashed value.
infra-bot: notice: collector config v2 deployed to canaries at 1802501200.
Jorge: thanks infra-bot. how about our retention sampling? suggestion: keep full spans for 0.1% of requests, keep metadata+hashed attrs for 100%, and keep prompt fragments (first 40 chars hashed) at 0.5% for long-term.
Anika: can we use reservoir sampling on a per-customer basis so low-volume customers don't get drowned?
Sam: yes, per-tenant reservoir sampling + global epsilon reservoir to protect QA traces.
Mia: here's a short sample config suggestion to discuss:
```
telemetry.ingest:
  push_hashed_ids: true
  id_salt_version: "v3"
  retention:
    raw_prompt_days: 7
    full_span_sample_rate: 0.001
    longterm_prompt_sample_rate: 0.005
  signature_prefix_len: 10  # hex chars
  admin_unseal_required: true
```
Lee: two asks: add a canary tag so we can route sampled full-spans to a qa index, and add an option to set per-customer override via feature flag.
Mia: both doable. we'll prototype in canary collector and dashboard the delta in storage cost.
ProductSRE: make sure dashboards show both 'effective unique keys' and 'estimated collision rate' so product teams understand the tradeoff.
Jorge: also add a metric for 'admin-unseal uses' and 'backfill rehash jobs' to monitor ops churn.
Mia: I'll open a doc + PR with the collector patches and sampling operator config. want ppl to review before EOD Friday. tagging @Lee @Anika @Sam @Jorge for review :thumbsup:.
